Wikipedia and PeakVisor both place Mount Claywood in Jefferson County, inside Olympic National Park. Washington law (RCW 38.52.400) makes the chief law enforcement officer of the political subdivision (the county sheriff) responsible for local search and rescue, so the county SAR named in the notes should be Jefferson, matching emergency.county.

results.fact: Distance to Spike Camp junction and Flapjack Lakes
results.evidence: Sources genuinely spread: the trail page gives 3.7 mi to the junction and 15.4 mi round trip (7.7 mi) to the lakes; a hiking blog gives about 3.5 mi then about 4 mi; a measured 2023 trip report gives 7.2 mi to the lakes; other listings give 3.4-3.6 mi to the junction and 7.45 mi to the lakes. No two independent sources agree on one figure, and the bivy copy (3.4 mi / 7.5 mi) is owned by the camping clean-up. Settling it needs the official park trail mileage for the North Fork Skokomish and Flapjack Lakes trails.

The line from Needle Pass angles up northeast onto Beta Peak and then follows the crest north to Cruiser's south side; the approach/baseFinding describe the first leg (turn left/east to Beta Peak) and the beta describes the crest trending north, so both are partial descriptions of one northeast-trending line.
